title: Build the first event-sourced ontology vertical in CyberAlchemy Lab
outcome: Deliver in the new CyberAlchemy-lab repository one small ontology whose canonical typed events deterministically calculate ontology_at(cursor), checked machine and human projections, and exact governance joins, with the implementation constructed through DomainSpec v2 under CAV2-D65 and bound to an exact Rust realization before any conformance, migration, or stable-version claim.
rationale: CyberAlchemy needs one stable ontology model instead of competing static graphs, snapshots, and hand-maintained indexes. The first vertical must prove that append-only events can calculate one consistent ontology state while DomainSpec governs the system design and exact implementation boundary without becoming the runtime event store or granting authority by generation.
scope: the CyberAlchemy-lab repository as the only implementation target for this Goal
one owner-selected Lab-native witness with two ontology nodes and one relation
one canonical semantic event stream per node or relation and one graph-wide monotonic commit cursor
typed events that carry complete resulting subject state
one Rust reducer and ontology_at(cursor) consistent-cut query
checked-in machine and human projections that can be deleted and rebuilt
separate governance event streams joined by exact semantic event identity, digest, and cursor
the complete CAV2-D65 construction sequence, with DomainSpec v2 enforced as the implementation method rather than treated as optional documentation
exclusions: using event-derived projections, latest snapshots, indexes, or validation summaries as canonical ontology source
starting DomainSpec or Rust work before definitions, Product Capability, business ontology, source epoch, and compiler-profile blockers close
claiming that deterministic compilation alone admits a system ontology or accepts an implementation
legacy ontology migration before the Lab-native witness closes
distributed writers, network services, deployment, publication, or stable v1.0.0 release in the first vertical
owner_route: CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle Project owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus DomainSpec v2 owner plus CyberAlchemy Lab ontology runtime owner

success_conditions.statement: The new CyberAlchemy Lab target has one schema-valid proposed Project and one linked draft Goal bound to the exact selected event-sourced ontology decision.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The Project and Goal close bidirectionally, appear in the Goal ontology view, name ../CyberAlchemy-lab as the target, preserve exact decision evidence, and retain authority_effect none.

success_conditions.statement: Canonical definitions, the parent Product Capability, and the Ontology Lifecycle business ontology establish the exact semantic predecessors for construction.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Every required term is reused or owner-resolved, the Product Capability and business ontology have exact identities and digests, and all DomainSpec nodes and relations trace to that meaning.

success_conditions.statement: DomainSpec v2 deterministically compiles the exact authored source to one graph and one source-bound system ontology before implementation.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: An admitted profile, current registries, exact compiler identity, two-run byte equality, graph receipt, system-ontology receipt, and business-system bridge all close without hand-authored competing projections.

success_conditions.statement: The exact Rust realization reconstructs the same ontology_at(cursor) state from canonical events across clean repeated replays.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Replay, cursor-gap, duplicate-event, invalid-subject, invalid-relation-endpoint, and incomplete-cut tests bind exact event fixtures, code symbols, tool versions, outputs, and receipts.

success_conditions.statement: Semantic and governance streams remain separate and join only through exact event identity, digest, and cursor.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Positive and negative runtime evidence proves correct joins and rejects wrong identity, digest, cursor, authority escalation, and unresolved governance references.

success_conditions.statement: Machine state, human views, indexes, and latest snapshots remain rebuildable calculated projections rather than competing ontology authority.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Deleting all projections and snapshots and replaying the same canonical events reproduces byte-identical outputs and current source-bound receipts.

success_conditions.statement: Legacy migration remains blocked until the Lab-native witness and its exact D65 construction and conformance evidence are owner-accepted.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The migration inventory has no admitted cutover record before witness acceptance, and every later imported record preserves source, provenance, residue, and an explicit owner decision.

evidence_requirements: Every D65 transition must preserve exact predecessor identities, versions, digests, owner routes, stage states, evidence, challenge routes, and drift routes.
The DomainSpec compiler and ontology reducer must have separate deterministic receipts because they transform different canonical inputs.
Every relation endpoint must resolve in the same ontology_at(cursor) cut.
A passing compiler, schema, unit test, replay, or validator must not imply ontology admission, implementation acceptance, Goal achievement, migration authority, release, or deployment.
Descriptions should use controlled, direct language while canonical ontology terms retain their exact owner-governed meanings.

evidence_refs.claim_limit: Supports the exact selected design and target only; it grants no construction, implementation, conformance, governance, migration, release, or deployment authority.
Supports the current blocker and layer map only; the recorded result is BLOCK and is not implementation readiness or authorization.

target_horizon: first Lab-native event-sourced ontology witness before legacy migration; no release deadline

revision_history.change: Created the Project and Goal, targeted the new CyberAlchemy-lab repository, bound the selected event-sourced design, and preserved the blocked D65 construction frontier.
revision_history.owner_route: CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle Project owner

challenge_route: Challenge the desired product result and target through the CyberAlchemy Lab Ontology Lifecycle Project owner, product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner, DomainSpec source and compilation claims through the DomainSpec v2 owner, runtime evidence through the CyberAlchemy Lab ontology runtime owner, and migration or release claims through their separate exact owner gates.
